beats.say: This worm can drink 8 times its weight in your blood.
It bites through your skin with three tiny jaws.
Its spit numbs you, so you don't feel it.
And hirudin keeps you bleeding for hours.
Doctors still use them. On purpose.
In the 1830s, Europe used about 60 million leeches a year.
One London hospital used 97,300 in a single year.
Then medicine moved on. Until surgeons brought them back.
When a finger gets sewn back on, blood can flow in, but not out.
It swells with trapped blood, and the finger can die.
So doctors put a leech on it, to drink the extra blood.
Its spit has more than 100 different chemicals in it.
In 2004, the US cleared leeches as a medical device.
The medicinal leech. A slimy worm with a sucker at each end.
One of those chemicals, hirudin, stops your blood from clotting.
So after it drops off, the bite can keep oozing for up to 48 hours.
Its small front sucker does the feeding, with those three jaws.
Doctors use them on sewn-back fingers, ears and even lips.
The worm you'd scream at in a pond is saving fingers in hospitals. Because
